lesson_body:
Welcome to Day 4 of our Counting Base unit, Grade 1 students! Today, we will dive deeper into counting, focusing on understanding how we can group numbers to make counting easier and more fun. You’ve already learned about counting from 1 to 20, and now we will explore how to count in groups of ten, which will help us see how larger numbers are made. 

First, let’s start with an engaging story! Imagine you discovered a treasure chest filled with colorful marbles. There are red, blue, and yellow marbles. As you look closer, you notice that there are 10 red marbles, 10 blue marbles, and 10 yellow marbles. Instead of counting each individual marble, we can group them! By knowing there are 10 in each color, we can say there are 30 marbles altogether without counting each one. 

Now, let's practice grouping! On your desks, there are blocks in sets of ten. We’ll start by counting each set together. As we count, I want you to shout out "10" every time we reach a new set of ten. For example, if we have two sets, we can say, "10, 20"! This is how we begin to understand larger numbers by using groups. This grouping technique is going to make your counting much faster, and you will be surprised at how many more numbers you can count! 

Next, let’s create our own number line! We will use the classroom wall to create a giant number line from 0 to 100. With your partner, you will grab sticky notes and place them on the number line according to the numbers you count while skipping by tens! Remember to say each number out loud: "10, 20, 30," and so on. This way, our entire class can visualize how counting in groups works while having fun together. 

As we wrap up, I will ask you to recall what we learned today! Count out loud with me, and let’s remember that counting in groups not only helps us with numbers but makes our learning quicker and enjoyable! You are doing such an amazing job, and I can't wait to see how you use this counting technique in our next lesson.
interactive_assignment:
For today's hands-on activity, you will make your own 'Counting Treasure Map!' On a large piece of paper, draw a treasure map that leads to three different 'treasure chests.' Each treasure chest should hold a different number of gold coins (disks or stickers). For each treasure chest, group your coins in sets of ten. Label how many you have in total for each group. You should have: 
1. A chest with 2 groups of 10 (20 coins) 
2. A chest with 3 groups of 10 (30 coins) 
3. A chest with 1 group of 10 and 5 single coins (15 coins) 
Once you finish your map, present it to the class and explain how you grouped your coins in sets of ten. This will help everyone understand how counting can be fun and useful!

daily_assessment.question: How many marbles are there in total if you have 4 groups of 10? What number do you say when you reach 40 by counting by tens?
